reference_evidence.reason: The authorized target screenshot was rediscovered outside the repository; only its filename and digest are frozen here.

items.expected_visual_effect: Readable base, shoulder, elbow, wrist and end-effector hierarchy at thumbnail scale.
items.finding: The serial hierarchy reads, but the silhouette remains more schematic and less integrated than the target.

items.expected_visual_effect: A grounded, compact service base with nested armor levels rather than stacked raw boxes.
items.finding: Iteration 68 replaces the three vertically extruded base layers and the large beveled turntable box with four bounded, hash-pinned vertical Loft shells. Their shared hard-edged octagonal section language creates closed bottom armor, outward bumper lips, tapered shoulders and a smaller upper turntable enclosure; the fixed views show nested product armor instead of raw stacked boxes. Local service panels and ring integration remain simpler than the target, but the layered enclosure is now present in the real GLB and no longer a blocking omission.

items.expected_visual_effect: Joint hubs carry believable mass while links taper continuously between them.
items.finding: Iteration 45 reduces the joint profile, bearing, core and guard radii while exposing paired upper/lower guards. Link-to-hub proportion is less disc-dominated in the isometric view, but the front view still exposes abrupt concentric transitions and overbright bearing faces.

items.expected_visual_effect: Open rails and braces create mechanically legible depth instead of solid slab arms.
items.finding: Negative space is present, but rails are visually thin and the braces do not yet form a coherent load-path language.

items.expected_visual_effect: A clearly readable three-finger concept gripper with a continuous palm and protected wrist.
items.finding: Iteration 24 makes all three fingers readable in the fixed front view and replaces thin wedges with bounded box-to-bevel distal shells; articulation quality remains tracked separately.

items.expected_visual_effect: Concentric bearing, paint and trim layers make the base rotation assembly legible.
items.finding: The rings read, but their material separation is too bright and uniform.

items.expected_visual_effect: Outer shell, bearing, inner core, guard and signal center read as nested functional-looking visual layers.
items.finding: Iteration 45 uses a darker graphite outer ring, smaller painted bearing face, reduced core stack and paired guards. The nested hierarchy is real and read back, but neutral front lighting still flattens several layers into bright concentric discs.

items.expected_visual_effect: Painted armor panels overlap a darker inner frame with clear seams and changing curvature.
items.finding: Iteration 54 replaces each formerly continuous painted side plate with three independently lofted, proportion-varying segments on both sides. Real gaps, an independent composite tension rod, an aluminum end cap and the darker shared-section inner shell remain readable in iso, left and right views; local curvature is still simpler than the target, but armor segmentation itself is no longer missing.

items.expected_visual_effect: Root and tip collars visually bridge rectangular rails into circular joints.
items.finding: Iteration 69 enlarges the two bounded painted Loft collars and overlaps them with the circular end guards. Fixed and development close views now show a real tapered shoulder at both ends of each link instead of a rail terminating directly at a disc. The transition remains simpler than the reference, but the previously missing bridge is present in the compiled GLB and no longer blocks the draft.

items.expected_visual_effect: Two controlled cable runs follow the arm with plausible slack and no floating segments.
items.finding: Iteration 23 lowers the harness toward the inner link; the run is now structurally adjacent, while endpoint integration still needs refinement.

items.expected_visual_effect: Clamps visibly attach the cable bundle to a structural rail.
items.finding: Iteration 23 reduces the clamp and places it beside the rail, removing the dominant floating-block defect.

items.expected_visual_effect: Maintenance covers and corner guards break up the base without looking decorative-only.
items.finding: C111B adds a dedicated beveled aluminum maintenance cover as a real Shape output and stable service-panel Material Zone alongside the existing corner guards. Its final target-image readability remains subject to the fixed-view visual gate.

items.expected_visual_effect: A layered wrist collar protects the palm transition and avoids a bare cylinder-to-box join.
items.finding: Iteration 66 replaces the short cylindrical guard with a bounded revolved graphite shroud, extends the painted inner sleeve into the palm, and repositions the revolved collar so all three layers overlap. Gripper close views no longer expose the former bare disc-to-palm gap; local surfacing remains simpler than the target but the protected wrist transition is now present.

items.expected_visual_effect: The palm changes section continuously and provides a designed mounting volume for three knuckles.
items.finding: Iteration 47 retains the compact 142 mm three-section Loft palm beside the smaller dedicated wrist. The continuous palm is read back and better proportioned, but it remains visually under-articulated.

items.expected_visual_effect: Each finger has a readable knuckle, protected proximal segment and substantial distal contact tip.
items.finding: Iteration 67 replaces the three exposed thin Sweep bodies with bounded beveled armor segments that overlap the revolved proximal knuckles and the short distal tips. Narrow graphite and rubber Sweep rails remain as surface accents and preserve the contact Material Zone; the two gripper close views show a continuous palm-to-knuckle-to-finger chain. Contact-pad surfacing and hinge layering remain simpler than the target, but the former disconnected transition is no longer a blocking omission.

items.expected_visual_effect: Restrained blue signal strips guide the eye without flattening the primary forms.
items.finding: Signals are visible but need finer placement and less uniform brightness.

items.expected_visual_effect: Small fasteners establish assembly scale around joint guards.
items.finding: Fasteners exist but have weak legibility at the full-asset camera distance.

items.expected_visual_effect: Panel gaps and normal grooves add scale without requiring dense geometry everywhere.
items.finding: Iteration 70 shortens all six painted Loft armor segments without changing the bounded output count. The real dark inner shell is now exposed as two stable recessed gaps per face on both links, while the two shallow graphite/composite inserts add a second panel-break scale and A005 retains exact-lineage normal-groove PBR. Fixed and close views show the panel language from both sides without the rejected blade-like protrusions. Micro relief remains below the target reference, but panel seams and grooves are no longer a missing critical layer.

items.expected_visual_effect: A bounded flowline motif reinforces the base perimeter.
items.finding: The five-channel texture lineage is proven, but the motif is subtle in the current lighting.

items.expected_visual_effect: A restrained microgrid differentiates painted joint surfaces from bare metal.
items.finding: Readback proves the program, while the full-view render does not yet prove strong material readability.

items.expected_visual_effect: Longitudinal lines emphasize arm direction and panel curvature.
items.finding: The output exists but reads as a generic bright stripe rather than a layered surface treatment.

items.expected_visual_effect: Chevron relief adds grip-scale structure to the dark palm shell.
items.finding: The normal pattern appears, but it repeats uniformly and does not compensate for weak finger geometry.

items.expected_visual_effect: A separate paint-zone microgrid differentiates the palm armor from graphite structure.
items.finding: Iteration 47 preserves balanced gripper microgrid lineage across the compact palm and swept finger paint zone. Readback remains stable, but the paint response and limited palm surface area keep the pattern visually modest.

items.expected_visual_effect: Paint, graphite, brushed metal, rubber contact and emissive trim remain distinguishable under neutral lighting.
items.finding: Iteration 58 binds five-channel 1K PBR across 155 primitives and embeds the versioned low-energy V2 studio contract. Dark graphite, matte composite, blue paint, aluminum, rubber and emissive trim remain distinguishable in the fixed views without the earlier pale base clipping; richer authored wear remains tracked separately.

items.expected_visual_effect: Sparse identifiers, warning marks and service labels establish believable product scale.
items.finding: C111B seals a narrow warning stripe and deterministic A-01 panel label into the retained link-armor Surface Layer; the same lowering is consumed by the five-channel GLB material and verified during readback.

items.expected_visual_effect: Very restrained edge wear and roughness variation prevent a uniformly new plastic appearance.
items.finding: C111B retains restrained edge wear and a 90-degree directional linear-brush roughness mask on the link-armor zone; exact lowering and five PBR map hashes are preserved in GLB provenance.

items.expected_visual_effect: Production GLB carries 1K five-channel PBR plus complete normal, UV0 and tangent data.
items.finding: Delivery channels pass deterministically; content richness and target similarity remain below the visual gate.
